title: Repeating Efficiently
outcome: By the end, I can check a loop condition before each update and count iterations.
scenario: A fictional paper counter advances through a display until its condition becomes false.
given: Start at 2. While the current counter is below 10, add 3.
Test before each addition; report when the condition is false.

steps.label: Stop test
steps.detail: 11<10 is false; do not add again.

explanation: The condition checks whether to do the next update; it does not constrain every resulting value to stay below 10. The final 11 is therefore allowed by this procedure. Record both the condition and counter to distinguish a correct stop from an assumed endpoint.

counterfactual.prediction: The loop runs zero times and reports 10.
counterfactual.reason: Its first condition is already false, so no addition happens.

student_task: Trace a fresh start of 9. How many additions occur, and must the report equal 10?
teacher_answer: 9<10 is true, so it becomes 12. Then 12<10 is false: one addition, report 12; equality with 10 is not required.
project_evidence: Give any repeated sorter step an explicit stopping condition and trace a zero-iteration example.
limits: This loop stops because positive increments eventually cross the limit. Other updates can fail to make progress.
review_note: New fictional worked case reviewed against the weekly topic and reserved independent assessment. Keep that assessment separate; this picture is supported practice.
